Betwixt
bē-twikst'
prep. (between; rendering Hebrew ben, Greek metaxu)
From Saxon betweox, related to two — the space or relation between two parties. The Authorized Version uses it interchangeably with between, and it clusters remarkably in Genesis, where it is the word of covenants made between men and witnessed by God.

Biblical Definition

Betwixt is simply between, but in the Authorized Version it falls almost entirely in the patriarchal narratives, where it becomes the preposition of covenant. Circumcision is given as “a token of the covenant betwixt me and you” (Genesis 17:11) — a sign cut into the body of every male, marking a bond that a man carries whether he thinks of it or not. When Jacob and Laban part after twenty years of mutual suspicion, they raise a heap of stones and swear over it, and the word recurs four times in a single chapter: “God is witness betwixt me and thee” (Genesis 31:50), “this heap, and behold this pillar, which I have cast betwixt me and thee” (Genesis 31:51), “The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor... judge betwixt us” (Genesis 31:53). Two men who do not trust each other invoke God as the third party to their treaty, which is what an oath is for. Ephron uses it more lightly, waving away the price of a burial field: “what is that betwixt me and thee?” (Genesis 23:15).

Webster 1828 Definition

A preposition meaning between — in the space or the relation dividing two parties. In Scripture it is the word of covenant: the token betwixt God and Abraham, and the heap of witness betwixt Jacob and Laban.

expand to see more

BETWIXT, prep. [Sax. betweox, from twa, two.] Between; in the intermediate space.

2. From one to another, noting passage or relation; as, a covenant betwixt them.

3. It is used of two parties only; among is used of more than two.

4. It is now less common than between, and belongs chiefly to the older and scriptural style.

5. In Scripture, a token of the covenant betwixt me and you, Gen. 17; God is witness betwixt me and thee, Gen. 31.

Key Scripture

Genesis 17:11 — "And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you."

Genesis 31:50 — "If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take other wives beside my daughters, no man is with us; see, God is witness betwixt me and thee."

Genesis 31:53 — "The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge betwixt us. And Jacob sware by the fear of his father Isaac."

Genesis 23:15 — "My lord, hearken unto me: the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver; what is that betwixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead."

Modern Corruption

Covenant has been reduced to contract — an agreement between parties for mutual advantage, dissolvable when the advantage ends. Scripture's covenants are sworn before God, sealed with a sign, and binding whether or not they remain convenient.

expand to see more

The difference shows most plainly in marriage. A contract is an exchange of considerations and ends when one party defaults or when both prefer to stop; a covenant is a bond made before God, who is named as witness and judge. Malachi says exactly this — the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy covenant — and it is the ground on which he condemns the treachery of divorce. The modern reduction of marriage to a terminable arrangement between consenting adults is not a development of the biblical idea but its replacement.

Genesis 31 shows the machinery of a covenant plainly, and it is worth noticing what is present: two parties who have every reason to distrust each other, a physical sign that will outlast the conversation, an oath naming God as judge, and a meal eaten together. The circumcision covenant of Genesis 17 has the same elements at a higher level, with God Himself as one of the parties and the sign cut into the flesh. Where covenant is understood, obligation does not depend on continuing goodwill; where it is not, nothing does.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ben, between, is often repeated before each party (between me and between thee), an idiom the translators smooth into a single preposition; Greek uses metaxu. The Saxon root is twa, two.

expand to see more

Hebrew ben (H996) — between, among; regularly repeated before each party in a covenant formula.

Hebrew berith (H1285) — a covenant, treaty, or alliance; the bond made betwixt the parties.

Hebrew 'oth (H226) — a sign or token; circumcision as the mark of the Abrahamic covenant.

Hebrew 'ed (H5707) — a witness; God invoked as the third party at Mizpah.

Greek metaxu (G3342) — between, in the midst; the New Testament preposition of the same sense.

Usage

"Of the sign of the Abrahamic covenant: a token of the covenant betwixt me and you (Genesis 17:11)."

"Of God invoked as witness between two suspicious parties: God is witness betwixt me and thee (Genesis 31:50)."

"Of a price waved away in courtesy: what is that betwixt me and thee? (Genesis 23:15)."
